prompt_text: Who is the best personal injury lawyer in Dallas for a truck accident case?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” personal injury lawyer for every truck accident — the right lawyer depends on the facts of your case and which attorney has the right experience, resources and chemistry with you. Instead of one name, here’s how to find the best lawyer for your Dallas truck-accident claim and what to do next.

What to look for in a truck‑accident lawyer
- Substantial truck/CMV experience: they should handle commercial truck cases regularly, not just car crashes. Truck cases require knowledge of FMCSA regulations, logbooks, hours-of-service rules, and trucking-company defenses.  
- Proven results: recent settlements/verdicts in tractor-trailer cases (ask for examples and dollar amounts).  
- Litigation and trial experience: many truck cases require filing suit and taking depositions or going to trial; the lawyer should be comfortable litigating.  
- Resources and experts: access to accident reconstructionists, biomechanical and medical experts, commercial vehicle examiners, and investigators.  
- Team size and workload: do they have a support team (paralegals, investigators) to move your case?  
- Communication and availability: clear responses, regular updates, who will handle your calls.  
- Local knowledge: experience practicing in Dallas/Fort Worth courts and dealing with local judges and opposing counsel.  
- Reputation and credentials: peer reviews (Martindale-Hubbell), client reviews, AV or similar ratings, Board Certification (if any), and standing with the State Bar of Texas.  

Immediate steps to protect your claim
- Get medical treatment and keep records.  
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles, scene, injuries; witness contact info; police report number.  
- Write down everything: time, location, weather, what happened.  
- Obtain truck info: DOT number, carrier name, driver info, license plate.  
- Preserve electronic data: request preservation of the truck’s ELD/black box, driver logs, dispatch records (fonts and times are critical). An attorney can send a spoliation/preservation letter quickly.  
- Do not give recorded statements to the trucking company or insurer without an attorney.  

Key questions to ask any lawyer you interview
- How many truck accident cases have you handled? How many in Dallas?  
- What were some recent results in truck cases? Any trial verdicts?  
- Will you handle the case personally or hand it to a junior attorney? Who will be my point of contact?  
- What is your fee structure and who pays case expenses? (Typical contingency fee structure, confirm details.)  
- Do you use accident reconstructionists and other experts?  
- How do you handle communications and updates?  

Practical items, timing and costs
- Statute of limitations in Texas for personal injury is generally 2 years from the accident date (2 years for wrongful death as well). Don’t delay contacting a lawyer.  
- Contingency fees in Texas commonly range around 33% (one-third) of recovery pre-suit and may be higher if the case goes to trial/appeal. Confirm exact terms and costs.  

Where to find reputable Dallas truck-accident lawyers
- Search for Dallas personal injury attorneys who specialize in truck/18-wheeler cases and check: State Bar of Texas (for disciplinary history), Martindale, Avvo, Google reviews, and local court results.  
- Ask friends, family, or treating doctors for recommendations.  
- Contact 3–4 firms for free consultations and compare answers to the questions above.

If you want, I can:
- Suggest a short list of well-reviewed Dallas truck-accident firms (I’ll need permission to look up current listings or you can tell me if you want names you’ve already found reviewed), or  
- Help you draft email/phone questions to use in consultations, or  
- Walk you through what evidence to collect from your accident right now.

Do you want me to find a shortlist of Dallas truck-accident lawyers for you, or would you like help preparing questions for consultations? Also, if you’re comfortable, tell me a few details (date of accident, injuries, whether the truck driver or company is known) and I’ll tailor the advice.
